name: South Dakota

creditorClaims.text: The published notice gives creditors 4 months after first publication; known creditors must be notified and have the later of 4 months after appointment or 60 days after the written notice (SDCL 29A-3-801); all pre-death claims are barred 3 years after death (SDCL 29A-3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 4 months after original appointment of a general personal representative (SDCL 29A-3-1003).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000, no personal representative is pending or appointed, and the decedent owes no Medicaid institutional-care debt to the Department of Social Services (SDCL 29A-3-1201). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (SDCL 29A-3-1201); summary administration proceedings ($25 clerk fee, SDCL 16-2-29(3)(i)); closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (SDCL 29A-3-1003).

filingFee.text: Clerk of courts fee of $75 for the probate of an estate; $25 for summary or special administration proceedings (SDCL 16-2-29).

personalRepFee.text: Personal representatives are entitled to reasonable compensation determined from seven listed factors, including time, difficulty, customary local fees and the nature and value of the assets (SDCL 29A-3-719(a)).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys, accountants and other agents of the personal representative are entitled to reasonable compensation under the same factors (SDCL 29A-3-719(a)); reviewable by the court (SDCL 29A-3-721).
